objective: Separate the extremal equality characterization from its edge bound; derive the short-cycle gap and an exact odd-order endpoint residual, and prove an elementary shortest-cycle MC lemma.

atomic_claims.text: Nontrivial ABC graphs have a cycle of length at most four; conditional on T3 and TABC, a simple no-MC graph of girth >=5 has m>=ceil(3(n-1)/2)+1.
On n>=2, maximum degree <=3 and girth >=5 suffice for MC, by an elementary shortest-cycle cut argument.
Conditional on T3 and TABC, any n>=2 no-MC graph of girth >=5 and average degree <3 has odd n>=9, 2m=3n-1, and t=1+sum(degree-3 over vertices of degree >=4)>=2.
The primary 2006 thesis abstract explicitly requires a nonempty proper shore for an edge cut, but does not authorize changing the OPG quantifier.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs, nonempty shores and possibly empty crossing matching.
Every positive subsidiary MC statement concerns n>=2; K1 remains in the frozen root.
T3 and the distinct extremal equality characterization TABC are attributed pending dependencies, not added axioms.
C07.2's shortest-cycle proof and the local counting arguments do not require T3 or TABC.
risks: ambiguous_problem_contract remains nonterminal; no root upgrade.
An exact extremal characterization does not cover graphs one edge above its bound.
The odd-order endpoint conditions are necessary only, not a witness or a general absence result.
The shortest-cycle argument needs the actual maximum-degree condition, not average degree <3.
Primary abstracts and conference text were read; the linked thesis PDF and full Wiley proof were inaccessible.
